specFirst: Written BEFORE the code, per skills/agentsBestPractices.md §1. This file, spec.md and the per-step CHANGELOG.md are the design record — there is no other document to look for. The decisions were closed with the product owner on 2026-08-19 and are restated in decisions[] below; when behaviour must change, change this file first, then the code.
description: EXPERIMENTAL PROBE (the pilot that closes the molecule-catalog analysis, §11). Given a page/system definition in prose, it walks the three-level molecule catalog and answers which GROUP and which MOLECULE serve each region of the page. It measures the catalog, not the page: it writes no molecule, no usage contract, no page — only measurement artifacts in l4. After the pilot it either becomes the real consumer (the page12 foreseen in agentChangeFrontend) or is absorbed by it.
principles: REUSE THE PLUMBING. Intents, l4 artifacts, stor mechanics and the strict tool wrapper come from agentNewMolecule2/helpers (nmFs, nmSteps) and shared/llmTool, never reimplemented. The catalog is read the way this family reads every file — from the stor (nmFs.readStorText) — with the published module as the fallback; see conventions.catalogRead for why that order, which the first Studio run decided.

ONE CATALOG LEVEL PER PROMPT. c1 sees level 1 (the groups) and c2 sees level 2 of ONE group. Never both, never two groups in the same call — the precedent is the 58 KB prompt that brought down i3-edit (the catalog analysis §2).

THE CATALOG IS THE ONLY SOURCE OF TAGS. Never a usage contract example (measured on 2026-08-19: 38 of their 40 example tags do not exist, across 29 of 31 groups), never the model's memory. A tag outside the group's published list is refused by a deterministic gate.

HONESTY IS AN ANSWER, NOT A FAILURE. A region no published group covers gets group: null; a region no molecule of the chosen group serves gets tag: null. Both need a reason. Inventing a plausible neighbour is the failure mode being measured.

THE REPORT IS MECHANICAL. c3 spends no LLM call: it aggregates what the two steps measured and renders it. A summary written by a model would be a fourth call polluting the token measurement, and it could describe a metric nobody took.

decisions.battery: Runs in the Studio, by hand: one mention per case of the 10-case battery in the pilot battery §3, plus 3 repetitions of cases #4 and #5 (the combobox × autocomplete tie).
decisions.modelType: reasoning + x-tool-strict on both LLM steps, per skills/modelTypes.md ('planning, comparing alternatives, multi-step decisions') and the family precedent (i2-triage, n2-plan). No reasoningEffort: c2 is a fan-out of small items. classifier stays as a second-round experiment.
decisions.fanOut: One c2 step per chosen group, planted in a second phase by the root, because the number of groups is unknown until c1 answers.
decisions.tagSpelling: The FULL prefixed tag ('groupselectone--ml-card-selector') is required. The gate refuses a bare short name instead of completing it: copying the tag exactly is part of what the pilot measures.
decisions.scoring: Manual. The agent never sees the battery's expected answers — a probe that knew them would be measuring itself. The scoring input is report.json.
decisions.tokens: TWO numbers, and they answer different questions. (1) The ASSEMBLED PROMPT, in chars with tokens estimated at 4 chars/token and the catalog block measured apart: that is what the three-level design is about, and it was the approved reading of the §11.4 criterion on 2026-08-19. (2) The REAL usage of the call, corrected on 2026-08-21: the platform does expose it, not in the step contract but as a line the runtime appends to interaction.trace (inputTokens / outputTokens / cost), so it is parsed and recorded per attempt. The gap is the point: c1 assembled 1.203 estimated tokens and the provider counted 7.727 of input, so the platform adds ~6x on its own (Content Memory, tool schema, thread context) and the real consumer pays that, not the estimate.

conventions.input: Prose from the mention: '@@agentChooseMolecules <definition of the page, screen or region>', optionally preceded by '{ catalogProject: N }'. Parsed by helpers/chEntry, never by mls.common.safeParseArgs, which throws on anything that is not an object literal — here the object is optional and the prose follows it.
conventions.catalogProject: EXACTLY ONE catalog answers a run, and which one is discovered: the search set is the ACTIVE project plus its DIRECT dependencies (prj_dependencies from the project settings, never the transitive list — a client that depends on a theme must not be offered the base library through it), and a project qualifies by having l2/molecules/skill.ts. One candidate is used; none, or more than one, is a readable refusal naming what it looked at. An optional '{ catalogProject: N }' before the prose overrides the search, which is what makes probing a theme catalog from outside it possible. Level 2 is never looked up: c1 pins each chosen group's indexDefs reference in its artifact, so the c2 steps read the same catalog c1 answered from. Recorded per run: the chosen project, how it was chosen, the candidates and both dependency lists.
conventions.catalogOneNotMany: Refusing on two reachable catalogs is deliberate. Molecules of two themes do not belong in the same page, so picking one in silence would answer with the wrong aesthetic and the run would still look correct. The refusal carries the argument that resolves it. A clarification with checkboxes and a UNION of catalogs is the agreed phase 2, triggered by the day a theme project gets a catalog of its own — today only one project has one, so a selection widget would show a single checkbox in every run.
conventions.catalogRead: THE STOR FIRST, the published module second — inverted on 2026-08-19 after the first Studio run. Rung 1 reads the file from the stor and turns its text into values with the pure helpers/chExtract (it parses only what the gates need and evaluates nothing): that is the source of truth inside the editor, and it is how every other agent of this family reads a file. Rung 2 is await import(reference), the gesture of readGroupSkill, which is served by the PUBLISHED project — the only rung a consumer that is not the editor has, and the one that needs no parser. Reasons for the order, both measured: an unpublished catalog is invisible to the import (level 2 died on Failed to fetch on the first run), and a published catalog with unsaved edits is read STALE by it without saying so. Which rung answered is recorded per level and surfaced in report.json.
conventions.writesNothing: No source artifact is written or edited. Not the molecule, not the usage.ts/creation.ts (manual by decision of 2026-08-17), not the group index, not the page. Only l4 measurement artifacts.
conventions.regionJoin: The region NAME is the join key between the two steps: c1 names the regions, c2 echoes them verbatim. A choice for an unknown region is a gate failure, because it cannot be joined.
conventions.runFolder: ONE FOLDER PER RUN, SEQUENCED (helpers/chTypes.chUniqueRunKey, wired in the root and nowhere else). The runKey is derived from the definition, so two runs of the same page produced the same l4 folder and the second OVERWROTE the first in silence. Measured on 2026-09-04: a re-run of cadastro-usuarios took the pre-amendment baseline with it, and only the fs trash got it back — luck, not design. The report is the only thing a probe run produces, so losing the previous one loses the comparison the run existed to make. The FIRST run of a slug keeps the clean name (an existing folder is never renamed, so a scored run stays where it was left); from the second on, -02, -03 ... is appended, budgeted inside nmRunKey's 40-character cap because the slug is also a file path, and refused out loud at 99 rather than wrapping around. input.json is the marker of a claimed folder because c1 writes it on attempt 1: a run that died before that measured nothing, so reusing its slug loses nothing. Decided ONCE, in the root's first phase — every step receives the runKey in its args and c1 puts it in task memory, so no step recomputes it.
conventions.regionGranularity: A CAPABILITY IS NOT A REGION, and the verbs it costs go into the need line instead (c1 prompt, 2026-09-04). Superdecomposition is this step's recurrent defect, measured three times: V1 promoted the table's row selection to a region of its own and got two components for one element of the screen; V5 promoted 'and saves'; the cadastro-usuarios run promoted all four CRUD verbs, which left the listing region reading as 'display a collection' and routed it away from the table group whose level 2 has a scenario row for exactly that flow. The counterexample that fixes the trigger is M1 ('WITH quantity editing in the cell'), which was not promoted: the trigger is the capability arriving as a VERB. So the rule has two halves that only work together — the prompt refuses a region per verb, AND the need line must carry whether the collection is only read or also maintained (created/edited/deleted) and where one record opens (in the row, in a panel beside the list, in a screen of its own, the vocabulary of the record-detail axis analysis). Information moves, it is never dropped: the need line is the only channel c2 has. NOT GATED — region count cannot be checked without an opinion about the choice, which is what the run measures. And it does not fix the level-1 line of the table group, which spends half its budget on slot tags and says nothing about maintaining a record (the catalog analysis §12.7, a GENERATOR fix); while c1 returns a single group per region (§12.3), an error of its own stays invisible and final. AMENDED THE SAME DAY (run crud-cadastro-usuario): the rule had swallowed the record's FIELDS too — a definition naming name/date of birth/e-mail/active came back as one region with the fields as prose in the need line, and the chosen molecule declares that the page owns the VALUES, so nothing would compose. The culprit was the positive criterion ('something the user fills, picks or reads that is not content of its neighbour'), written for actions: a field in a cell IS content of its neighbour. Separated now — a CAPABILITY needs no component and is not a region; NESTED CONTENT needs one and stays a region. A named field of a record the user maintains is a region, with two limits against the opposite overshoot: columns of a collection the user only reads are not regions, and a field the definition does not name is never invented. This is a HEURISTIC whose flaw is ORDER — whether a field needs a molecule depends on the container molecule, known only after c2, so the signal is taken from the definition, not from the molecule. The structural fix is a region with parent + slot (schema, gate and rows[] all change) and it belongs to agentChooseMolecules2, which already has that shape from a typed contract. THIRD AMENDMENT, same day: a field region's need line must also name the RECORD it belongs to ('field of a record of the <collection> collection'), because the c2 that picks the field never sees the collection's region and density is exactly what separates the siblings of the entry groups — measured on the run that followed the second amendment, where a yes/no field of a maintained collection got the form-sized sibling over the dense one, and a birth date got the standard picker over the space-constrained calendar. The line says the CONTEXT and never the layout: writing cell, panel or screen into it is forbidden, because where the record is edited depends on the container molecule, chosen a call later. CORRECTED on the next run: the clause DISPLACED the field's own facts instead of adding to them — all four field need lines came back interchangeable but for the type word, and 'of birth' left the line that decides typing over a calendar 30 years back (no damage that run only because c2 also sees the region NAME). The culprit was 'say no more than that', written against layout and read as the scope of the whole line; it now carries ALSO / 'never in place of them', a right-wrong example pair, a swap test (two fields of one record whose need lines could trade places have lines too thin), and the layout ban moved to its own paragraph. AND THE CLAUSE IS ON PROBATION: it has changed no choice yet. c2 read 'a record of the users collection' as 'a registration form' and used it to CONFIRM the form-sized siblings, the opposite of the prediction; density could never have come from here, since naming a cell or a screen is forbidden. The real gap is editorial — neither groupEnterBoolean nor groupEnterDate has a scenario row for a field rendered in the data row of a collection (§12.6), so c2 chose well within what it was offered. If the clause still changes nothing after the correction, remove it and recover the characters.
conventions.retry: One retry with the gate errors in the prompt (CH_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2). A c2 that still fails records ok: false and COMPLETES — the run's product is the measurement, and 'the model insisted on an invented tag' is a result, not a crash.

treeOverview: c0-classify (the root's own call: slug, language, titles)
c1-groups            level 1 -> regions and their groups
c1r-fanout           the root again: plants one c2 per chosen group, plus c3
c2-<group>         level 2 of that group -> the molecule per region
c3-report            mechanical: report.json + the readable summary

steps.agentName: agentChooseMolecules (the root itself — no separate step agent)
steps.goal: Cheap classifier over the prose: does it describe something a UI has to do? Propose the runKey slug, detect userLanguage and localize the step titles. It must NOT name a group, a molecule or a tag — the whole point of the probe is that those come from the catalog, one level at a time. A SINGLE region is valid input (measured on 2026-08-20: it was being refused, and 6 of the 10 battery cases are phrased that way) — refusing produces no measurement, while a region nothing covers is answered honestly with none.

output.result: { validInput, reason, runKey, userLanguage, title, titles }

steps.doneAnchor: none (the root plants the tree directly)

steps.goal: Break the definition into REGIONS (each an interaction a molecule could serve) and name, for each, the group that covers it or null.
input: the definition, in the human prompt

checks: every region carries a need and a reason
gate.onFail: retry 1 with the errors in the prompt; a 2nd failure fails the step

steps.goal: Read c1's answer and plant one c2 step per DISTINCT group, plus c3 depending on all of them. With no group chosen it plants c3 alone — the honest empty report, which is what battery case #10 exercises.
For ONE group: choose the molecule for each region c1 assigned to it, plus which quick-reference scenario was used.
input: level 2 of the group (mod.skill of its index.defs.ts)
the regions of this group, in the human prompt

checks: THE ANTI-INVENTION CHECK: every tag belongs to mod.molecules[].tag of THIS group, spelled in full
a bare short name is refused with the full tag in the message
the group matches the step's group
every region belongs to this group's list, and none is left unanswered
scenarioUsed belongs to mod.scenarios[].scenario or is null
tag null is allowed with a reason
gate.onFail: retry 1 with the errors in the prompt; a 2nd failure records ok: false and completes

steps.goal: Aggregate the run: entry, both steps' outputs, prompt sizes per step (with the catalog block apart), gate verdicts and how many times the anti-invention gate fired. Write report.json and render the readable summary.

output.result: the summary, in the step trace

artifacts.l4/agentChooseMolecules/<runKey>/input.j: the definition as it arrived, the runKey, the language and the level-1 reference
artifacts.l4/agentChooseMolecules/<runKey>/c1-grou: the regions with their group (or null) and reason
artifacts.l4/agentChooseMolecules/<runKey>/c2-<gro: the choices of one group, with ok and the gate history
artifacts.l4/agentChooseMolecules/<runKey>/prompt-: the size of the prompt assembled on attempt NN, split into instructions / catalog / input
artifacts.l4/agentChooseMolecules/<runKey>/trace-<: the gate verdict of attempt NN
the consolidated run — this is the file the battery is scored from. NOT named run.json: a file by that name in this folder was found holding a TaskData dump written by something else

acceptance.battery: the 10 page definitions of the pilot control, one run each, scored by hand against its gabarito
acceptance.moleculeHitRate: a clear majority (c2), each miss analysed: the agent's fault or the catalog's?
acceptance.inventedTags: ZERO reaches an artifact. Every time the gate fires is recorded in report.json — the gate holding is not the same as the model getting it right.
acceptance.honesty: case #10 answers group: null on both regions, with no plausible neighbour invented
acceptance.tie: case #4 (combobox × autocomplete): if it misses consistently, the registered fallback is a contrastive sentence in the source # Objective of the tied molecules — never a new keywords field (decision of 2026-08-19)
acceptance.promptSize: level 1 ~387 estimated tokens and level 2 between 505 and 1452 per group, measured on the seeded files on 2026-08-19; the run confirms the assembled prompt stays in that order of magnitude

outOfScope: writing or fixing usage.ts / creation.ts (manual — decision of 2026-08-17; the defective examples are tracked by their own control, outside this project)
n7-index / i6-index / v4-index and the indexGroupPage skill — including inverting the scenarios table (§11.5)
the keywords field (decided against on 2026-08-19: risk of superficial vocabulary matching)
the local theme / 102054 (second round) and the 26 groups outside the pilot
writing the page: this probe chooses, it does not compose
planting: Two phases, for the reason agentImproveMolecule2 has a router: the branch is not known when the tree is planted. Phase 1 (root afterPromptStep) plants c1 and the fan-out step. Phase 2 (root beforePromptStep on c1r-fanout) reads c1's result and plants the c2 steps plus c3. c3 depends on the c2 anchors by NAME, all of which were planted in the same batch — never on a shared 'c2-done', which would be an anchor several steps write.
